gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the maker's runtime claim for the Anker SOLIX EverFrost 2 40L works out to about 5.5 W average draw (288 Wh for 52 h, empty, Eco mode, 39°F setpoint, 77°F ambient), while the Koolatron W65 that ChatGPT showed is rated at 60 W and its maker only promises 40°F below the outside air. Nor does any result say that the 'Dual-Compartment' second zone on the $269.99 BODEGACOOLER card is not set on its own: its temperature is 'influenced by the primary zone'.
standout_why: I compared GearJunkie (2026-10-31), GiftSitter (2026-10-08) and lovethe88 wheeled (2026-11-09). GearJunkie and GiftSitter already say that thermoelectric coolers cool about 40°F below ambient, and GiftSitter applies that to the Koolatron W65, so that part is not new. GearJunkie gives the EverFrost 2 40 'up to 36 h at 39°F' but no ambient temperature and no watts. Its FAQ only gives a general 40 to 70 W range. GiftSitter gives watts for one product, the BougeRV CR28 (ECO ~45 W, MAX 60 W), and those are rated figures, not averages. None of the three turns a runtime claim into average watts, gives Anker's 77°F test ambient, or puts Koolatron's 60 W next to it. GiftSitter lists a 'BODEGA 40L Dual-Zone' as having independent zones. None of the three says that the cheaper BODEGACOOLER dual-compartment model ChatGPT carded has a dependent second zone. The page's new fact is the normalised table. Rivals already cover part of it, which is why I scored 2 rather than 3.
decides: This confirms that the pick should be a compressor cooler, and it removes the Koolatron for anyone running on a battery. The maker figures work out to roughly 11× more power (60 W rated against 5.5 W average). At Anker's own 77°F test ambient, Koolatron's 40°F-below claim reaches only about 37°F. At 90°F it reaches about 50°F, well above the 39°F Anker tested at. The BODEGACOOLER finding makes ChatGPT's top card ($269.99, 'Dual compartments') weaker for anyone who wants a fridge and a freezer at the same time. BODEGA's own independent ('true dual-zone') 40L costs $569.99 and showed as out of stock. On our list, the EverFrost 2 40L is the cooler with wheels whose efficiency claim states its test conditions.
